description: This topic explains the meaning and classification of industries, the factors influencing where manufacturing industries are located, types of manufacturing, industrialisation in Tanzania, the importance and problems of industries, and their effects on the environment.

mcq.questionText: What does the term 'manufacturing' mean in geography?

options.text: Growing crops for sale in the market
Changing raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods
Extracting minerals from the ground
Providing services such as banking and transport

mcq.explanation: Manufacturing is the processing or changing of raw materials into finished or semi-finished products using machines and labour.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a primary industry?

options.text: A textile mill in Dar es Salaam
A bank in Arusha
Mining of gold at Geita
A cement factory at Wazo Hill

mcq.explanation: Primary industries extract or collect raw materials directly from nature, such as mining, fishing, farming and forestry.

mcq.questionText: Secondary industries are best described as those that:

options.text: Provide services to people
Process raw materials into manufactured goods
Extract raw materials from the environment
Sell goods directly to consumers only

mcq.explanation: Secondary industries take the raw materials from primary industries and turn them into finished goods, so manufacturing belongs here.

mcq.questionText: A heavy industry is one that:

options.text: Uses bulky raw materials and produces large, heavy products
Employs only a few workers in homes
Produces small, light goods such as watches
Requires very little capital to start

mcq.explanation: Heavy industries, such as iron and steel or cement, use bulky raw materials, large machines and produce heavy products.

mcq.questionText: Which industry is an example of a cottage or small-scale industry in Tanzania?

options.text: An oil refinery
Hand weaving of baskets and mats
A large vehicle assembly plant
A steel rolling mill

mcq.explanation: Cottage industries are small-scale, often done at home with simple tools, such as weaving baskets, pottery and tailoring.

mcq.questionText: Which factor most strongly attracts a sugar factory to be located near a sugarcane farm?

options.text: Availability of skilled labour
Nearness to perishable and bulky raw materials
Government tax policy
Availability of a large market

mcq.explanation: Sugarcane is bulky and perishable, so the factory is built near the farm to reduce transport cost and avoid spoilage, as at Kilombero.

mcq.questionText: Why are many industries located close to large towns and cities?

options.text: To be far from raw materials
To avoid paying any taxes
To be near a large market and available labour
Because land in towns is always free

mcq.explanation: Cities offer a big market for goods and a large supply of labour, which encourages industries to locate there, as in Dar es Salaam.

mcq.questionText: The cement industry at Wazo Hill near Dar es Salaam is located there mainly because of:

options.text: Cool climate for cement drying
Availability of limestone raw material nearby
A large lake for fishing
Cheap imported raw materials only

mcq.explanation: Cement is made mainly from limestone, so cement factories are built near limestone deposits such as those at Wazo Hill.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an agro-processing industry?

options.text: A cashew nut processing factory at Mtwara
A gold mine at Geita
A hydro-electric power station
A motor vehicle assembly plant

mcq.explanation: Agro-processing industries process agricultural products, such as cashew nuts, cotton, sisal and coffee, into useful goods.

mcq.questionText: Which power source is most commonly used to run manufacturing industries in Tanzania?

options.text: Wind energy
Geothermal energy
Hydro-electric power and natural gas
Nuclear energy

mcq.explanation: Tanzanian industries rely largely on hydro-electric power and natural gas, such as gas from Mnazi Bay and Songo Songo.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of manufacturing industries to a developing country?

options.text: Creation of employment
Earning foreign exchange through exports
Increased air and water pollution
Adding value to local raw materials

mcq.explanation: Pollution is a negative effect of industries, not a benefit; the others are real advantages of industrialisation.

mcq.questionText: A major problem facing industries in developing countries like Tanzania is:

options.text: Too much capital available
Shortage of capital and unreliable power supply
Excess of skilled engineers
Very low demand for any goods

mcq.explanation: Developing countries often suffer from limited capital, unreliable electricity, poor technology and competition from imports.

mcq.questionText: An assembly industry is one that:

options.text: Extracts raw minerals from the ground
Puts together ready-made parts to form a product
Grows food crops for processing
Provides transport services only

mcq.explanation: Assembly industries join together manufactured parts, for example motor vehicle and bicycle assembly plants.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is widely used as a cleaner source of industrial energy in Tanzania?

options.text: Natural gas from Songo Songo and Mnazi Bay
Helium from Lake Natron
Imported coal gas only
Hydrogen from Lake Victoria

mcq.explanation: Tanzania has natural gas deposits at Songo Songo and Mnazi Bay, used for electricity generation and industry.

mcq.questionText: Compared with an industrialised country such as Japan, Tanzania's manufacturing sector is characterised by:

options.text: More advanced technology and higher output
Mostly light, processing industries with limited heavy industry
A larger steel and car industry than Japan
No dependence on imported machinery

mcq.explanation: Tanzania is at an early stage of industrialisation, dominated by light processing industries, while Japan has advanced heavy and high-tech industries.

fib.questionText: An industry that extracts raw materials directly from nature, such as mining and fishing, is called a _____ industry.
fib.explanation: Primary industries collect or extract natural raw materials before any processing takes place.

fib.questionText: Industries that change raw materials into manufactured goods are known as _____ industries.
fib.explanation: Secondary industries process raw materials into finished or semi-finished products.

fib.questionText: Industries that provide services rather than goods, such as banking and tourism, are called _____ industries.
fib.explanation: Tertiary industries offer services like transport, trade, education and health.

fib.questionText: The main raw material used to make cement is _____.
fib.explanation: Cement factories such as Wazo Hill are located near limestone deposits because limestone is the chief raw material.

fib.questionText: A small industry carried out at home using simple tools, such as basket weaving, is called a _____ industry.
fib.explanation: Cottage industries are small-scale and use simple equipment, often within the home.

fib.questionText: The Kilombero factory in Tanzania is mainly known for processing _____ into sugar.
fib.explanation: Kilombero Sugar Company processes sugarcane grown nearby because the crop is bulky and perishable.

fib.questionText: Industries that use bulky raw materials and produce heavy products, like iron and steel, are called _____ industries.
fib.explanation: Heavy industries handle large, bulky materials and require large machines and capital.

fib.questionText: Money invested to start and run an industry, including buildings and machines, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Capital is needed to buy machinery, land and raw materials; shortage of capital limits industries in developing countries.

fib.questionText: Industries that process farm products such as cotton, coffee and cashew nuts are called _____ industries.
fib.explanation: Agro-processing or agro-based industries depend on agricultural produce as their raw materials.

fib.questionText: Government rules and incentives that encourage industries to set up in certain areas are known as government _____.
fib.explanation: Government policy, through taxes, subsidies and special zones, influences where industries are located.

tf.questionText: Manufacturing is the process of changing raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods.
tf.explanation: This is the correct definition of manufacturing.

tf.questionText: Mining of minerals is an example of a secondary industry.
tf.explanation: Mining is a primary industry because it extracts raw materials directly from nature.

tf.questionText: Light industries usually produce small and light goods such as textiles, soap and matches.
tf.explanation: Light industries make light, less bulky products and need less capital than heavy industries.

tf.questionText: Availability of raw materials has no influence on where an industry is located.
tf.explanation: Raw materials are a major locating factor, especially when they are bulky or perishable.

tf.questionText: Most manufacturing industries in Tanzania are concentrated in Dar es Salaam.
tf.explanation: Dar es Salaam has the port, market, labour and power, so it hosts many of Tanzania's industries.

tf.questionText: Industries can help a country earn foreign exchange by exporting manufactured goods.
tf.explanation: Exporting processed goods brings in foreign currency and improves the economy.

tf.questionText: Air and water pollution are positive effects of manufacturing industries on the environment.
tf.explanation: Pollution of air, water and land is a negative environmental effect of industries.

tf.questionText: Unreliable power supply is one of the problems facing industries in developing countries.
tf.explanation: Frequent power cuts disrupt production and raise costs for industries in countries like Tanzania.

tf.questionText: Cement and iron and steel are examples of heavy industries.
tf.explanation: These industries use bulky materials, large plants and much capital, so they are heavy industries.

tf.questionText: Industrialised countries such as Japan depend mainly on cottage industries for their economy.
tf.explanation: Industrialised countries rely on large-scale, advanced heavy and high-tech industries, not mainly cottage industries.

summary.correctAnswer: An industry is any economic activity concerned with producing goods or providing services, including extracting, processing and selling.
summary.explanation: Industry covers all activities that produce goods or offer services to satisfy human needs.

summary.questionText: List the three main classes of industry by level of production.
summary.explanation: Industries are grouped into primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing) and tertiary (services).

summary.questionText: State two factors that influence the location of industries.
summary.correctAnswer: Availability of raw materials and a reliable source of power or energy.
summary.explanation: Other factors include labour, capital, market, transport, water, land and government policy.

summary.questionText: Give two examples of manufacturing industries found in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Textile industries and food processing industries such as sugar at Kilombero.
summary.explanation: Tanzania also has cement, beverage, agro-processing and cigarette industries.

summary.questionText: Differentiate between heavy and light industries.
summary.correctAnswer: Heavy industries use bulky materials and make large heavy goods, while light industries use lighter materials and make small light goods.
summary.explanation: Iron and steel are heavy industries; textiles and soap are light industries.

summary.questionText: Why are perishable raw materials important in deciding industry location?
summary.correctAnswer: Industries using perishable materials must locate near the source to process them quickly before they spoil.
summary.explanation: Examples include sugar, fruit and dairy industries located close to farms.

summary.questionText: State three benefits of manufacturing industries to Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: They create employment, earn foreign exchange and add value to local raw materials.
summary.explanation: Industries also reduce imports, develop skills and improve infrastructure.

summary.questionText: Mention three problems facing industries in developing countries.
summary.correctAnswer: Shortage of capital, unreliable power supply and poor or outdated technology.
summary.explanation: Other problems include competition from imports, low skilled labour and small markets.

summary.questionText: Describe two negative effects of industries on the environment.
summary.correctAnswer: They cause air pollution through smoke and water pollution through dumping of waste.
summary.explanation: Industries can also cause land degradation, noise pollution and deforestation.

summary.questionText: Give two differences between manufacturing in Tanzania and in an industrialised country.
summary.correctAnswer: Tanzania uses simple technology with mostly light processing industries, while industrialised countries use advanced technology with large heavy and high-tech industries.
summary.explanation: Industrialised countries also have more capital, skilled labour and higher output than Tanzania.

hoq.questionText: A new fruit-canning factory is to be built in Tanzania. Which location factor should be given top priority to reduce spoilage and transport cost?

options.text: Building far from the fruit farms in a big city centre
Locating near the fruit-growing area because fruit is perishable and bulky
Locating near a gold mine for cheap minerals
Locating on a mountain top for cool air

hoq.explanation: Perishable and bulky raw materials like fruit must be processed quickly, so the factory should be near the farms to cut spoilage and transport cost.

hoq.questionText: A region with cheap hydro-electric power, good roads and a nearby city wants to attract industries but has frequent power cuts. What is the best long-term solution?

options.text: Close the existing industries to save power
Invest in reliable and additional power sources such as natural gas and grid improvement
Ban all new industries from the region
Move all industries to areas with no roads

hoq.explanation: Reliable energy is essential for industry, so improving and diversifying power supply, for example using natural gas, solves the root problem of power cuts.

hoq.questionText: A factory near a town dumps untreated waste into a river used by villagers. Which response best balances development and environmental protection?

options.text: Allow the dumping to continue because the factory creates jobs
Require the factory to treat its waste before release and enforce pollution laws
Close all industries permanently to protect the river
Move the villagers away from the river instead

hoq.explanation: Sustainable development means keeping the jobs while protecting the environment, so treating waste and enforcing pollution control is the best balanced response.
